sentences.cn_text: 你是如何进行阅读的？
sentences.en_text: How does your reading proceed?

sentences.cn_text: 显然，你会努力理解文本，即识别单个词汇的含义并理清它们之间的关系，同时调用你对英语语法的隐性知识。
sentences.en_text: Clearly you try to comprehend, in the sense of identifying meanings for individual words and working out relationships between them, drawing on your implicit knowledge of English grammar.

sentences.cn_text: 你开始为文本推断语境，例如，通过判断涉及何种言语事件：谁在说话，对谁说话，何时何地说话。
sentences.en_text: You begin to infer a context for the text, for instance, by making decisions about what kind of speech event is involved: who is making the utterance, to whom, when and where.

sentences.cn_text: 这里所指的阅读方式无疑都属于理解的范畴。
sentences.en_text: The ways of reading indicated here are without doubt kinds of comprehension.

sentences.cn_text: 但它们表明，理解不仅包括被动的吸收，还包括积极参与推理和解决问题。
sentences.en_text: But they show comprehension to consist not just of passive assimilation but of active engagement in inference and problem-solving.

sentences.cn_text: 你推断出的信息，是你认为作者通过提供具体证据和线索而邀请你领会的。
sentences.en_text: You infer information you feel the writer has invited you to grasp by presenting you with specific evidence and clues.

sentences.cn_text: 如此理解，阅读理解对每个读者而言不会遵循完全相同的路径。
sentences.en_text: Conceived in this way, comprehension will not follow exactly the same track for each reader.

sentences.cn_text: 问题的关键不在于检索某个可以读取并核查准确性的绝对的、固定的或「真实」的意义，也不在于文本与世界之间某种永恒不变的关系。
sentences.en_text: What is in question is not the retrieval of an absolute, fixed or “true” meaning that can be read off and checked for accuracy, or some timeless relation of the text to the world.

sentences.cn_text: 这种背景材料不可避免地反映出我们的身份。
sentences.en_text: Such background material inevitably reflects who we are.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，这并不意味着解读仅仅是相对的，甚至是毫无意义的。
sentences.en_text: This doesn’t, however, make interpretation merely relative or even pointless.

sentences.cn_text: 正因为来自不同历史时期、地点和社会经历的读者对页面上相同的文字产生不同但又相互重叠的解读——包括对那些涉及人类基本关切的文本——围绕文本的辩论能够在社会对信仰和价值观的讨论中发挥重要作用。
sentences.en_text: Precisely because readers from different historical periods, places and social experiences produce different but overlapping readings of the same words on the page — including for texts that engage with fundamental human concerns — debates about texts can play an important role in social discussion of beliefs and values.

sentences.cn_text: 我们如何阅读某一特定文本，在一定程度上也取决于我们阅读它的特定兴趣。
sentences.en_text: How we read a given text also depends to some extent on our particular interest in reading it.

sentences.cn_text: 阅读的这些维度表明——正如本书后面介绍的其他维度也将表明——我们在任何阅读行为中都带有隐含的（往往未被承认的）预设立场。
sentences.en_text: Such dimensions of reading suggest — as others introduced later in the book will also do — that we bring an implicit (often unacknowledged) agenda to any act of reading.

sentences.cn_text: 由此并不必然得出结论：某种阅读方式比另一种更全面、更高级或更有价值。
sentences.en_text: It doesn’t then necessarily follow that one kind of reading is fuller, more advanced and more worthwhile than another.

sentences.cn_text: 理想状态下，不同类型的阅读相互启发，并作为有益的参照点和彼此的平衡力量。
sentences.en_text: Ideally, different kinds of reading inform each other, and act as useful reference points for and counterbalances to one another.

sentences.cn_text: 它们共同构成你整体读写能力中的阅读部分，或者说构成你与周围文本环境的关系。
sentences.en_text: Together, they make up the reading component of your overall literacy, or relationship to your surrounding textual environment.

sentences.cn_text: 我们是在研习该文本并试图以满足某门课程要求的方式作出回应吗？
sentences.en_text: Are we studying that text and trying to respond in a way that fulfils the requirement of a given course?

sentences.cn_text: 纯粹为了消遣而阅读它？
sentences.en_text: Reading it simply for pleasure?

sentences.cn_text: 快速浏览以获取信息？
sentences.en_text: Skimming it for information?

sentences.cn_text: 在火车上或床上的阅读方式很可能与在研讨室中的阅读方式大相径庭。
sentences.en_text: Ways of reading on a train or in bed are likely to differ considerably from reading in a seminar room.

sentences.cn_text: 诸如我们阅读的地点和时期、我们的性别、种族、年龄和社会阶层等因素，会引导我们倾向于某些解读，但同时也会使其他解读变得模糊甚至完全封闭。
sentences.en_text: Factors such as the place and period in which we are reading, our gender, ethnicity, age and social class will encourage us towards certain interpretations but at the same time obscure or even close off others.

sentences.cn_text: 如果你不熟悉某些词汇或习语，你会利用上下文提供的线索猜测其含义。
sentences.en_text: If you are unfamiliar with words or idioms, you guess at their meaning, using clues presented in the context.

sentences.cn_text: 基于它们以后会变得相关的假设，你会在脑海中记下话语实体以及它们之间可能存在的联系。
sentences.en_text: On the assumption that they will become relevant later, you make a mental note of discourse entities as well as possible links between them.

sentences.cn_text: 实际上，你试图重构任何特定句子、意象或引用可能具有的意义或效果：这些可能是作者意图传达的。
sentences.en_text: In effect, you try to reconstruct the likely meanings or effects that any given sentence, image or reference might have had: These might be the ones the author intended.

sentences.cn_text: 你作出进一步的推断，例如关于文本对你可能具有的意义，或关于其有效性的推断——这些推断构成个人回应的基础，而作者对此不可避免地承担更少的责任。
sentences.en_text: You make further inferences, for instance, about how the text may be significant to you, or about its validity — inferences that form the basis of a personal response for which the author will inevitably be far less responsible.

sentences.cn_text: 在戏剧、小说和叙事诗中，人物作为作者创造的构造物在说话，未必是作者自身思想的传声筒。
sentences.en_text: In plays, novels and narrative poems, characters speak as constructs created by the author, not necessarily as mouthpieces for the author’s own thoughts.

sentences.cn_text: 相反，我们基于所谓文本材料与语境材料之间的互动来赋予文本以意义：这种互动发生在我们对文本形式结构（尤其是其语言结构）中感知到的各种组织或模式，与我们带入文本的各种背景、社会知识、信念和态度之间。
sentences.en_text: Rather, we ascribe meanings to texts on the basis of interaction between what we might call textual and contextual material: between kinds of organization or patterning we perceive in a text’s formal structures (so especially its language structures) and various kinds of background, social knowledge, belief and attitude that we bring to the text.
